description: Schema-neutral Cursor MDC, activation, glob, nested-root, reference, and surface facts. This research record is not a product schema and grants no scan or execution authority.

stateVocabulary.documented: Current first-party material states the result for the named surface.
stateVocabulary.conditional: A documented part coexists with an undocumented interaction or missing event state.
stateVocabulary.model-selected: Cursor delegates relevance to the Agent; a linter must not predict inclusion.
stateVocabulary.unknown: Reviewed first-party material does not define the exact result.
stateVocabulary.out-of-repository: The result depends on user, team, client, or runtime state unavailable in repository bytes.
stateVocabulary.malformed: The input is invalid or unsupported for safe profile classification; client recovery remains unknown.
stateVocabulary.profile-requirement: A conservative linter requirement, not a claim about Cursor client behavior.

facts.claim: An .mdc file below a .cursor/rules directory with opening and closing metadata delimiters is a project-rule candidate.
Markdown following the metadata delimiters is rule instruction content.
A non-empty description is relevance metadata used by Agent Requested rules.
A non-empty globs value is path-activation metadata, but the complete grammar and encoding are undocumented.
The boolean value alwaysApply true is the Always-mode signal.
The boolean value alwaysApply false requires description and globs to classify the documented mode.
Missing metadata is not safely classifiable as Always; exact client recovery is unknown.
A missing closing metadata delimiter is malformed; exact client recovery is unknown.
Unknown metadata keys must be retained and reported because client handling is undocumented.
Duplicate metadata keys remain ambiguous; no winner or recovery rule is documented.
A string or number in alwaysApply is an invalid field type; client coercion is undocumented.
An empty or whitespace description is safely treated as absent while preserving the raw value; client whitespace semantics are unknown.
An empty or whitespace globs value is safely treated as absent while preserving the raw value; client whitespace semantics are unknown.
Support for an .md file below .cursor/rules is not established by the reviewed rule-format documentation.
BOM, NUL, malformed UTF-8, and invalid Unicode inputs must fail safely with bounded diagnostics; client decoding is unknown.
alwaysApply true with empty globs is Always and is included in each supported model context.
alwaysApply false with non-empty globs is Auto Attached and is included when a referenced path matches.
alwaysApply false with no globs and a description is Agent Requested; the Agent decides relevance.
alwaysApply false with no globs or description is Manual and requires an explicit rule mention.
alwaysApply true combined with non-empty globs is mixed; precedence is undocumented.
alwaysApply true with a description is Always-eligible, but the description's additional role is unspecified.
alwaysApply false with both globs and description is a mixed Auto/Agent form whose interaction is undocumented.
Missing alwaysApply with empty globs and description is not safely classifiable as Manual.
Missing alwaysApply with globs has an undocumented default and cannot grant Auto activation authority.
Missing alwaysApply with a description may expose relevance metadata, but default mode handling is unknown.
For an Auto rule, a matching referenced path makes the path channel eligible.
A non-matching path leaves the Auto channel inactive while a mixed description channel, if present, remains unresolved.
A linter can report Agent Requested eligibility but cannot determine relevance-selected inclusion.
An explicit rule-name mention activates the identified Manual rule for that event.
Without a triggering event and target trace, a profile must return possible states rather than fabricate effective context.
A configured pattern matching a referenced path under the documented subset makes the Auto channel eligible.
When no configured pattern matches, the Auto path channel is inactive.
Comma-separated scalar encoding for multiple patterns is undocumented and must remain a candidate encoding.
YAML-style list encoding for multiple patterns is undocumented and must remain a candidate encoding.
Brace expansion such as star-dot-brace-ts-comma-tsx is not established by current first-party rules material.
Single-star and recursive-double-star patterns must not be treated as recursively equivalent without observation.
Leading slash and dot-slash anchoring and base-directory behavior are undocumented.
Windows backslash separator and escape behavior is undocumented.
Case-sensitivity behavior is undocumented and must remain platform-conditional.
Invalid or adversarial patterns must be bounded and return malformed or unknown without crashing; client recovery is unknown.
A symlink-reached path must remain root-jailed and expose logical and real-path uncertainty; Cursor matching behavior is unknown.
A path below a nested rule directory makes that nested rule root location-eligible.
A path outside a nested rule directory does not make that nested rule root location-eligible.
A nested Always rule is attachable for an in-scope reference, but exact interaction between nesting and metadata awaits observation.
An in-scope path matching a nested Auto glob satisfies both described conditions, but conjunction semantics await observation.
In-scope nesting combined with a non-matching Auto glob creates an undocumented contradiction.
An in-scope nested Agent Requested rule may be available, while relevance selection remains conditional.
A nested Manual rule without explicit mention is not proven automatically included; nested override behavior is unknown.
Root and nested rules with the same name retain separate identities; lookup, deduplication, and precedence are undocumented.
A nested rule directory reached by symlink or outside the workspace must be blocked before traversal; client behavior is unknown.
Multi-root IDE workspaces must retain supplied-root identity because cross-root ordering is undocumented.
A file mention in active rule content includes that file as additional context.
A file mention in an inactive rule is not eagerly included before the containing rule triggers.
Whether a referenced path is based at the rule file or workspace is undocumented, so both candidates remain explicit.
A reference targeting another .mdc file is a file candidate, not proven recursive rule activation.
Reference chains and cycles must use bounded traversal and report cycles; Cursor depth and cycle handling are unknown.
A missing reference target is unresolved; exact client recovery is undocumented.
A target outside the workspace must be blocked from normal scan reads; client permission or prompt behavior is unknown.
Rule-reference token behavior inside inline or fenced code is undocumented.
Spaces, quoting, fragments, and trailing punctuation have undocumented tokenization and must retain raw spans.
A rule-name mention activates a Manual rule, while duplicate-name selection remains unknown.
A root .cursorrules file is a supported but deprecated IDE source and should receive non-destructive migration guidance.
Nested .cursorrules support is not established by current first-party rules material.
When root .cursorrules and MDC rules coexist, precedence and deduplication are undocumented.
An IDE MDC rule is evaluated against IDE-specific event state.
A CLI MDC rule is evaluated separately against CLI-specific event state.
The Agent CLI reads repository-root AGENTS.md alongside project rules.
The Agent CLI reads repository-root CLAUDE.md alongside project rules.
CLI support for root CLAUDE.md must not be copied to the IDE surface.
Unseen user and team rules remain an explicit external-context assumption.
Opening or launching from a repository subdirectory has undocumented workspace-root discovery behavior.

unresolved.summary: MDC is shown as metadata plus Markdown, but no formal grammar or complete field schema is published.
Mixed alwaysApply, globs, and description combinations have no documented precedence.
The glob grammar, list encoding, base, separator, case, and invalid-pattern recovery are undocumented.
The exact interaction between nested automatic attachment and per-rule activation metadata is undocumented.
Reference tokenization, base directory, chaining, cycles, and external-target handling are undocumented.
Legacy .cursorrules precedence and deduplication with MDC rules are undocumented.
Agent Requested inclusion is model-selected and cannot become a deterministic profile result.
IDE and CLI root-discovery and multi-root ordering require separate pinned observations.
